proofs.title: Ira M. Lapidus — A History of Islamic Societies, 2nd ed.
proofs.captureMethod: Complete seven-page PDF captured byte-for-byte. OCR unavailable; printed pp. 314–315 rendered and read visually; passage transcribed from p. 315.
proofs.locator: Printed pp. 314–315, Reconquista section; Granada and final conquest
proofs.passage: By the middle of the thirteenth century only Granada remained in Muslim hands. It was protected by a large populace, a mountainous territory, and a productive economy which paid heavy tribute to the princes of Castile. Aragon had turned its interests to the Mediterranean, Castile was embroiled in civil wars, and the military orders were disbanded. Christian rulers gave no priority to the conquest of Granada until the union of Castile and Aragon opened the way for the final conquest of the last Muslim possession in Spain in 1492.
